page.layout: Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Two portrait medallions side by side with legends around them, no text blocks. Below them one full-width column of running text (paragraph 1, then paragraph 2). No margin notes.

main_text.p: MENELAVS, Atrei (alij dicunt Plisthenis) & Aeropes filius, in uxorem accepit Helenam formosissimā quidem mulierem, attamē quæ bis rapta est, primùm à Thefeo, postea à Paride. Hic Menelaus regnauit apud Lacedæmonios anno mundi 2758. ante Christum natum 1204. aduersus Troianos bellum gessit pro recuperanda uxore, quam non nisi capta Troia recuperauit. bellum gessit decem fere annis. præterea conscendens nauim in reditu, non nisi post octauum erroris annum patriam attigit. Tantæ molis erat infame reducere scortū. scribit nihilominus Dictys Cretensis non tam animo consternatum fuisse Menelaum ob raptam uxorem, quàm ob Aetram & Clymenam, affines suas. Sustulit ex Helena Hermionem. Dares Phry. Ouid. lib. 11. Metamorp. Cæterùm Menelaum Atrei filium Homerus scribit, Hesiodus autem, Plisthenis.

AGAMEMNON regnauit Mycœnis anno mundi 2768. ante Christum natum 1194. hic frater fuit Menelai: & omnium consensu Græcorum dux præcipuus aduersus Troianos declaratus est: classem habuit nauium sexaginta supra centum: uniuersa Græcorum classis erat nauium plus mille. Tandem reuersus ab expeditione illa, & bello Troiano confecto, ipse, insidiis Clytemestræ uxoris, ab Aegystho adultero interfi-citur: Orestésque filius eius hanc iniuriā ulcisci-tur, interfectis adulteris, matre scilicet Clytemnestra ac Aegystho. Euripid. in Oreste, Seneca in Agamemnone. Dares Phrygi. Dictys Cre.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are copied from the engraved rings. The right legend is partly hidden by the curve of the medallion: "AGMEMNON" and "REX MYC" are my reading, and the end of the word is uncertain. Paragraph 1: "Clytemestræ" (paragraph 2) and "Clytenestræ" are the same name as printed. Some letters in the scan are faint, but the running text reads cleanly. No notes in the margins.
